transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I keep reliving that night at the front desk over and over in my head, like I’m back on the floor with a gun in my face and I can’t shut it off. It happened during an armed robbery at the hotel where I work, and I just can't seem to get past it.
How long ago did the robbery happen, and have these symptoms lasted more than a month? If they started right after it happened, are they still continuing now?

The robbery happened about three weeks ago, and these symptoms started a few days after it. It's been going on continuously for about two weeks now, so it hasn't been a full month yet, but it is still happening every single day.
Since the robbery, have your symptoms been getting better, staying about the same, or getting worse? Also, have there been any brief periods when you felt mostly back to normal?

They definitely aren't getting any better; if anything, it feels like they're getting worse and more intense every day. I haven't had any moments of feeling back to normal at all. It's just been a constant, exhausting struggle since it started.

Before this robbery, had you ever gone through another traumatic event that caused similar flashbacks, nightmares, or avoidance for more than a month? Or are all of these symptoms only related to this robbery from three weeks ago?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. All of these symptoms are completely new and only started after the robbery three weeks ago.

Since the robbery, have you had moments where you felt detached from yourself or like things around you weren’t real? Have you also had trouble remembering important parts of what happened during the robbery?

Yes, especially at the hotel, everything will suddenly feel fake and far away, like I'm watching myself from across the room and have to touch my arm or the counter to ground myself. But I don't have any trouble remembering the robbery itself—honestly, I remember it all too well and can't get the details out of my head.

Since the robbery, have you been avoiding reminders of it—like the front desk, talking about what happened, or thoughts about that night? Have you also been feeling constantly on edge, jumpy, or having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I actively avoid talking or thinking about it, and I've been dodging my night shifts and staying out of the lobby alone. I'm also incredibly on edge all the time—any sudden noise like a door slamming makes me jump out of my skin, leaving my heart racing and my hands shaking.

Since the robbery was three weeks ago, have these symptoms been present almost every day since then, and are you still within the first month after the event? If they continue past one month, please let me know.

Yes, they’ve been happening almost every single day for about two weeks now, starting just a few days after the robbery. Since the incident only happened three weeks ago, I’m definitely still within that first month.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed trauma-related symptoms within days of a qualifying life-threatening event (armed robbery with gun threat), including intrusive re-experiencing, avoidance, dissociative symptoms, and hyperarousal. Symptoms have been present nearly daily for about two weeks and the trauma occurred only three weeks ago, keeping the presentation within the first month, which supports acute stress reaction/disorder rather than PTSD.
